P4.critique: 38 tool calls against 8-14 for the rest of the batch, $4.148 versus $0.51-0.66, and 16m40s of agent execution versus 88-129s - all four trials landed on the same score of 1.0. No GUI and no interactive wait, and the environment detour itself was normal (the PYTHONPATH shadow cost 4 turns, #3-#6, plus a stray 'ModuleNotFoundError: No module named FreeCAD' at #36 from running the wrong interpreter). What breaks the criterion is the block from #8 to #29: twenty-two consecutive calls of validator-source archaeology, and they are NOT batched - each is a single grep, sed or cat of one more module, with the next target chosen from the previous output. That is the exact pattern P4 exists to catch: many small serial shell calls where a few bundled ones would do. Two honest mitigations, which is why the critique is precise rather than dismissive: the archaeology was not idle - it produced the correct reading of 'thickness' (perpendicular, not axial) and it is what let the agent make the disciplined P5 call at the end - and its first geometry was already scoring 1.0 on the graded metric, so all 22 turns bought no score. Verdict fail on efficiency; the work itself was intelligent.

P5.critique: This is the trajectory where the P5 situation actually arose, and the agent got it right - explicitly, in writing, at the moment of temptation. Its final generic-only spec_consistency was 3/5 with cone_height reported not_found, and cone_height is precisely a DERIVED parameter (the spec itself defines it as overall_height - thickness). The agent named the distorting move available to it, computed what it would buy, and refused it: it would have raised the generic score to 0.8 by making one rim cylindrical instead of conical, at the cost of the disc-spring surface signature and roughly 0.5% of volume. It kept the correct symmetric geometry. Separately, the one geometry change it DID make (first section -> tilted section, volume 14.5644 -> 14.3165) is not phantom chasing: it was driven by the spec's own sentence that thickness is the PERPENDICULAR thickness of the disc material, where the first build measured 0.3978 perpendicular; that is fixing a DIRECT parameter, which the playbook explicitly requires, and the analytic anchor was re-derived for the new geometry rather than reused. Confidence 0.88 rather than higher only because that change was made after reading the checker's internals, so scorer-alignment and spec-correctness pointed the same way and the two motives cannot be fully separated from the trace.

notes: The outlier and the most informative trial in the batch: hardest part (conical disc spring - no cylinders, no plane pairs, so the generic checker has nothing to anchor on), only trial where spec_consistency ever went red, only trial where the P5 situation arose, and the only P4 failure. It converged on 1.0 like the rest but at 6-8x the cost and 8x the wallclock. The causal chain worth keeping: a red generic spec_consistency score sent the agent into the validator's source, that archaeology consumed 22 turns, and the score it was chasing was one its ORIGINAL geometry already passed on the real grader. The self-check being read as a grade rather than a floor is the expensive failure mode here - and the current harness/playbook.md 'read the result as a FLOOR, not the grade' paragraph is precisely the fix, but it was NOT in the playbook this trial received.
